title: Marketplace bundle risk vs value playbook (WIP)
body:
Purpose
This is a working playbook to decide which SKU bundle permutations we will pursue for cloud marketplace listings (AWS/Azure/GCP) and the co-sell partner program. Goal is to capture trade-offs (value to customer, revenue/commission complexity, legal/entitlement risk, ops surface area), draft final marketplace copy variants, and produce a launch checklist that product/ops/finance can sign off.

Context / why now
- Several inbound partner requests to offer bundled entitlements (hosted API + dedicated credits + premium console observability) for large ISVs.
- Sales has identified that a simple "bundled-trial" offering increases trials by ~22% in our pilot verticals, but compliance and billing exceptions killed 2 pilots last quarter.
- Marketplace listings require explicit SKU mapping and trial entitlements per cloud vendor — we need a reproducible decision tree and copy bank to reduce rework.

Quick summary of bundle archetypes (working)
- Essentials bundle: hosted API credits + basic observability (7 day trial). Low friction, low legal risk.
- Scale bundle: reserved Dedicated capacity credits + priority support + 30 day trial (subject to approval). Higher revenue but billing complexity.
- Private-ready bundle: Private deployment license + onboarding hours + optional KMS setup. Requires contract amendment and onboarding SLA.
- Hybrid bundle (experimental): small dedicated caps + hosted bursting + per-customer data residency note. High operational surface.

Evaluation matrix (how to decide whether to offer a bundle)
- Customer Value (CV): Will this materially shorten sales cycles or increase ARR ACV? (H/M/L)
- Operational Complexity (OC): New billing types, SSO/KMS integration, entitlement enforcement (H/M/L)
- Legal/Compliance Risk (LCR): Data residency, export controls, custom contract terms (H/M/L)
- Marketplace Acceptance Risk (MAR): Special approvals needed by vendor or incompatible SKU model (H/M/L)
- Delta Margin (DM): Expected uplift in margin vs stand-alone SKU (percent estimate)

Decision heuristic (draft)
- If CV = H and LCR <= M and MAR <= M -> prioritize (move to pilot)
- If OC = H and DM < 15% -> deprioritize (too costly)
- If bundle requires contract change or PO-only billing -> escalate to Legal + Finance (JIRA-9876)

Checklist: Pre-listing requirements
- SKU mapping: unique SKU per cloud vendor + mapping doc (owner: Evan)
- Billing test: verify trial expiration flows + auto-upgrade path in sandbox (owner: Rina)
- Compliance signoff: Privacy & Security review (owner: Jamal)
- Marketplace metadata: tile copy, benefits, trial terms, support contact, asset images (owner: GTM content team)
- Legal: contract amendment templates for private-ready bundles (linked: CONFLUENCE-1234)

Launch gating items (must be green)
- Billing: automated provisioning + entitlement checks pass end-to-end in vendor sandbox
- Observability: telemetry surfaced in Redwood Console for token-level cost and latency for bundled customers
- Sales enablement: one-pager, demo script, price sheet, example contract clause
- Support runbook: installation/onboarding steps + escalation matrix for bundle-specific issues

Copy bank (short variants by usage)
- Tile headline (short): "Redwood Inference — Fast, predictable LLM inference (Bundled)"
- Tile subtitle (30–50 chars): "Hosted + Dedicated credits — start fast, scale reliably"
- Long description (marketing): "Ship LLM features with consistent latency and predictable cost. The Redwood Bundle combines hosted API credits for rapid prototyping with reserved dedicated capacity for production scale. Includes trial credits, priority onboarding, and observability tools to optimize inference cost and quality. Ideal for product teams building mission-critical LLM features across regulated environments."
- Benefit bullets (for tile): "Predictable performance; Fast prototype -> production path; Cost controls & observability; Optional private deployment"
- Quick support blurb: "Bundled customers receive priority onboarding and a dedicated technical contact for model and deployment guidance."

Vendor-specific note drafts (short)
- AWS: "Marketplace listing uses AMI-style entitlements for dedicated credits. Trial SKUs must expire cleanly — see sandbox test steps."
- Azure: "Offerings require a separate plans.json and SKU matrix. Need PM approval for co-sell eligibility."
- GCP: "Trial entitlements currently supported as promo codes — heavy coordination with partner ops."

Open questions / risks (todo)
- Entitlement enforcement: Can we unify enforcement across hosted + dedicated without custom billing connectors? (owner: infra team)
- Commissioning complexity: How will partner referral/commission be tracked for mixed consumption bundles? (owner: finance)
- Legal templates: What minimal contract language triggers manual review vs auto-accept? (owner: legal)
- Pricing strategy: Should bundles be discounted flat % or tiered based on committed capacity? (owner: product pricing)

Action items (next 2 weeks)
- Evan: produce vendor SKU mapping spreadsheet + sample SKU ids (due 2025-11-28)
- Rina: run end-to-end billing sandbox for AWS & Azure (due 2025-12-04)
- Jamal: privacy checklist and required DPA changes for private-ready bundle (due 2025-12-02)
- GTM content: finalize tile copy A/B variants and two hero images (due 2025-12-07)

Notes to self / rough ideas
- Consider a "trial-to-dedicated" migration flow that auto-allocates reserved capacity for customers who exceed X tokens/day — reduces churn and increases commit conversion.
- Keep a canonical mapping table in repo: /partner-assets/marketplace/schemas/sku-mapping.csv (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/partner-assets/pull/42)
- Slack thread: #marketplace-listings (see pinned message) contains vendor-specific template files and example merchant support emails.

Appendix: quick risk scoring template (copyable)
- Use a 1–5 scale per dimension (Customer Value, Operational Complexity, Legal Risk, Marketplace Risk, Delta Margin). Total > 14 -> requires C-level approval.

Annotated links / references
- CONFLUENCE-1234: existing marketplace SKU policy (draft)
- JIRA-9876: "Marketplace bundled billing exceptions" (epic)
- GitHub PR 42: sample sku mapping artifact

If you’re editing this doc: add notes inline and tag @Sofia (Sofia.Martinez@redwood.com). This is intentionally rough — main goal is to converge on an opinionated minimum viable set of bundles we can list without major legal/billing rework.
